ERA.title: The Executive Energy & Resilience Audit
ERA.intro: A diagnostic across cognitive load, physical strain, circadian health, workplace culture, and recovery environment — the same one used to map where energy is actually leaking, and what kind of reset would actually fix it, before recommending anything. There's no passing score. Everything happens in this browser tab; nothing is transmitted, stored, or seen by anyone else.

sections.name: Cognitive Load & Mental Stamina
sections.note: Executive function, decision fatigue, and focus preservation.

sections.name: Somatic & Ergonomic Load
sections.note: The physical toll of a sedentary desk environment on muscle and nervous system.

sections.name: Circadian Health & Energy Architecture
sections.note: Systemic exhaustion via sleep and biological rhythm disruption.

sections.name: Organizational Alignment & Culture
sections.note: Whether the environment around you supports wellness, or quietly sabotages it.

sections.name: Recovery Environment & Retreat Fit
sections.note: Whether you have a real way to decompress at all — and whether a change of setting would outperform it.

questions.label: Cognitive Recovery (Brain Fog)
questions.prompt: How frequently do you experience a noticeable drop in mental clarity, decision-making efficiency, or concentration before the workday ends?

options.label: Daily (typically by mid-afternoon)
2–3 times per week
Rarely — I maintain high cognitive stamina throughout the day

questions.label: Hyper-Vigilance & Adrenaline
questions.prompt: Do you find it difficult to emotionally or mentally “switch off” from work communications within two hours of completing your shift?

options.label: Yes — my mind remains actively engaged in work problems late into the night
Occasionally, depending on project cycles
No — I have a distinct psychological boundary between work and personal time

questions.label: Creative Resilience
questions.prompt: When faced with sudden project changes or high-pressure deadlines, how would you rate your internal capacity to adapt without feeling overwhelmed?

questions.label: Postural Decompression Fatigue
questions.prompt: Select the physical areas where you experience chronic tightness, dull aches, or pain during or immediately after the work week.

options.label: Cervical spine / upper trapezius — neck and shoulder stiffness
Lumbar region — lower back compression from sitting
Temporal / ocular strain — headaches or eye fatigue from screen glare
Wrist / carpal tunnel discomfort

questions.label: Somatic Movement Baseline
questions.prompt: On average, during an 8-hour workday, how often do you actively stand up, stretch, or change your physical environment?

options.label: Only during formal lunch/tea breaks (highly sedentary)
Every 2 to 3 hours
Every 60–90 minutes (optimal movement pattern)

questions.label: Sleep Architecture Validation
questions.prompt: Which statement most accurately describes your sleep quality over the past 14 days?

options.label: Disrupted — I experience sleep-onset latency (mind racing) or wake up frequently
Insufficient — I sleep uninterrupted but wake up feeling physically unrefreshed
Restorative — I achieve deep, consistent sleep and wake up naturally energized

questions.label: Stimulant Dependency
questions.prompt: To maintain baseline professional productivity, how heavily do you rely on external stimulants (caffeine, nicotine, sugar) throughout the day?

options.label: High dependency — 3+ servings required to avoid energy crashes
Moderate dependency — 1–2 servings out of habit
Low or no dependency — natural energy baseline

questions.label: Well-being Psychological Safety
questions.prompt: Do you feel that your immediate leadership team respects personal boundaries and actively encourages self-care practices?

options.label: No — prioritizing wellness is subtly perceived as a lack of professional commitment
It's spoken about conceptually, but operational metrics prioritize overwork
Yes — wellness is actively modeled by leadership

questions.label: Future Intervention Optimization
questions.prompt: If you could introduce one targeted wellness intervention into your work life, which would yield the highest immediate impact on your performance?

options.label: Nervous System Regulation — breathwork, anxiety management
Ergonomic & Physical Recovery — mobility drills, pain relief
Time-Management & Mindset — boundary setting, stress psychology

questions.label: Environmental Impact on Recovery
questions.prompt: When attempting to completely decompress from work stress, which setting do you feel rejuvenates your nervous system the fastest?

options.label: Nothing consistent — I don't have a real way to fully decompress from work stress right now
A controlled, indoor space — a wellness studio, gym, or quiet room at home
A natural, outdoor setting — greenery and open air, away from screens

questions.label: Outdoor Openness Baseline
questions.prompt: How willing would you be to participate in mindfulness, yoga, or sound healing sessions conducted in structured, scenic outdoor spaces (e.g., resort lawns, forest trails)?

options.label: Not really my thing — I'd rather do structured wellness activities indoors
Willing, with the right conditions — good weather, a comfortable space
Very open — outdoor, nature-based sessions genuinely appeal to me

questions.label: The Retreat Value Metric
questions.prompt: If your organization hosts an off-site wellness program, do you believe spending 3 days in a nature-led resort would improve your work morale and team connection more than a standard city-based workshop?

options.label: No — a change of location wouldn't move the needle much for me
Maybe — it could help, but I'm not certain it beats a well-run in-city session
Yes — a real change of scenery in nature would meaningfully outperform a city-based session

ERA_BANDS.name: Resilient
ERA_BANDS.copy: Your baseline is genuinely strong. The read below is mostly about protecting it.

ERA_BANDS.name: Stable
ERA_BANDS.copy: A solid foundation with a couple of clear cracks — worth patching before they widen.

ERA_BANDS.name: Strained
ERA_BANDS.copy: Real, accumulated load across more than one system. A few targeted changes would compound fast.

ERA_BANDS.name: Depleted
ERA_BANDS.copy: Multiple systems are running on empty at once. Start small, start with just one thing, start today.
